records.text: The Network Contagion Research Institute produced a report featuring Owens's face that claimed 'Christ is King' had become antisemitic, in partnership with Johnnie Moore and Jordan Peterson.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They were also the ones that came up with a report with my face on it claiming that Christ is King was suddenly anti-Semitic. ... And Dr. Jordan Peterson all trying to convince you in a psyop that if you think Christ is king, you might be falling for the dark tetrad.

verification.notes: The NCRI report exists, includes Jordan Peterson and Johnnie Moore among its authors, and discusses Candace Owens while arguing extremists weaponized the phrase Christ is King. The episode overstates the report by saying it claimed the phrase itself had become antisemitic; the report distinguishes ordinary religious use from extremist use.

sources.relevance: The NCRI report itself establishes its authors, treatment of Owens, and narrower claim that extremists weaponized the phrase.

records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: He's just responding naturally. The PR guy. Anyway, it's entitled permission to kill. Look, kill is in red. Ooh, they're serious guys. ... Focus groups sat down and said, let's put the word kill in red. And they have obviously a target's gunshot and then a scope looking at someone and it says, how Candace Owens built a digital assassination culture targeting Erika Kirk.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The contemporaneous publication identifies the NCRI document by the exact title 'Permission to Kill: The Three-Phase Campaign to Legitimize Violence Against Candace Owens.'

records.text: Owens said NCRI had previously promoted the claim that 'Christ is King' was antisemitic and released that report during Lent.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: They do focused reports on, I think, really just me, things that I say. And they were really pushing and pedaling a couple years ago that Christ is King is anti-Semitic. They released this report during Lent. It backfired, obviously.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The March 13, 2025 NCRI report documented extremist and antisemitic actors weaponizing the phrase 'Christ is King'; it did not classify the Christian profession itself as inherently antisemitic. The report was released during Lent, which began March 5, 2025. The statement is therefore accurate about timing and the controversy but overstates the report's conclusion.

records.text: Owens said Kirk strongly criticized the NCRI 'Christ is King' report while Johnnie Moore sat on NCRI's board.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: Chief among people who were very critical of this report was Charlie Kirk himself. And Charlie didn't care that the NCRI had Johnnie Moore on their board, Andrew Kolvet's old partner, Johnnie Moore on the board of NCRI when the Christ is King report was published.

verification.notes: The NCRI report and Johnnie Moore’s co-authorship are public, but searches did not locate a reliable primary record of Kirk’s alleged strong criticism or establish that Moore sat on NCRI’s board when the report was published.

records.text: Owens said the NCRI report accusing her of being a digital assassin was published on the first day of Tyler Robinson's trial.
records.speaker: Candace Owens

appearances.snippet: This twerp, look at him. And then he also was a part, of course, of this report that was published about me accusing me on the day, the first day of a Tyler Robinson trial of being a digital assassin.

verification.notes: Transcript context reviewed. The NCRI report titled 'Permission to Kill' was publicly reported on July 8, 2026, immediately after the July 6 opening of Tyler Robinson's preliminary hearing. Calling that proceeding the first day of his 'trial' is inaccurate: it was a preliminary hearing, not a trial.
